chapterTitle: The Lamb on Mount Zion, Three Angels and Two Harvests
themeTitle: “Blessed Are the Dead Who Die in the Lord”

scripture.text: I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him a number, one hundred forty-four thousand, having his name, and the name of his Father, written on their foreheads.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ ἀρνίον ἑστὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σιών, “I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); ἀρνίον, from the lamb family. After the dragon on the seashore (13:1) comes the Lamb on the mountain of God: Psalm 2's King set on Zion. καὶ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, “and with him a number, one hundred forty-four thousand” — the sealed of 7:4: God's whole people, complete. ἔχουσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένον ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν, “having his name, and the name of his Father, written on their foreheads” — the answer to the beast's mark: they belong to the Lamb and the Father.

scripture.text: I heard a sound from heaven, like the sound of many waters, and like the sound of a great thunder. The sound which I heard was like that of harpists playing on their harps.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῆς μεγάλης, “I heard a sound from heaven, like the sound of many waters, and like the sound of a great thunder” — φωνή, voice or sound: the voice of Christ in 1:15. καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς κιθαρῳδῶν κιθαριζόντων ἐν ταῖς κιθάραις αὐτῶν, “The sound which I heard was like that of harpists playing on their harps” — overwhelming power and exquisite beauty together.

scripture.text: They sing a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn the song except the one hundred forty-four thousand, those who had been redeemed out of the earth.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ᾄδουσιν ὡς ᾠδὴν καινὴν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, “They sing a new song before the throne” — καινός, from the new family: new in kind, the song of redemption (5:9). καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο μαθεῖν τὴν ᾠδὴν εἰ μὴ αἱ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, “No one could learn the song except the one hundred forty-four thousand” — δύναμαι, from the power family; μανθάνω, to learn: only those who have experienced redemption can sing of it. οἱ ἠγορασμένοι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, “those who had been redeemed out of the earth” — ἀγοράζω, from the redeem family: bought out of the marketplace the beast controls (13:17); γῆ, from the world family.

scripture.text: These are those who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were redeemed by Jesus from among men, the first fruits to God and to the Lamb.
scripture.understanding: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἳ μετὰ γυναικῶν οὐκ ἐμολύνθησαν, παρθένοι γάρ εἰσιν, “These are those who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins” — παρθένος. In the prophets, idolatry is adultery; Paul presents the church to Christ ‘as a pure virgin’. The strongest reading is spiritual faithfulness — men and women who have not prostituted themselves to the beast and Babylon (17:1–5) — rather than literal celibacy. οὗτοι οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπου ἂν ὑπάγῃ, “These are those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes” — ἀρνίον, from the lamb family: the essence of discipleship, even to the cross. οὗτοι ἠγοράσθησαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρχὴ τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ, “These were redeemed by Jesus from among men, the first fruits to God and to the Lamb” — ἀγοράζω, from the redeem family; ἀπαρχή, the first sheaf of the harvest, offered to God as a pledge of the rest.

scripture.text: In their mouth was found no lie, for they are blameless.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν οὐχ εὑρέθη ψεῦδος, “In their mouth was found no lie” — ψεῦδος: they did not join the great lie of the beast and the false prophet, nor say ‘Caesar is Lord’. Zephaniah promised that the remnant of Israel would ‘not speak lies’. ἄμωμοί εἰσιν, “for they are blameless” — ἄμωμος, without blemish: the word for a perfect sacrificial animal, like the Lamb Himself.

scripture.text: I saw an angel flying in mid heaven, having an eternal Good News to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth, and to every nation, tribe, language, and people.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον πετόμενον ἐν μεσουρανήματι, “I saw an angel flying in mid heaven” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). Most manuscripts read ‘another angel’. Where the eagle cried ‘Woe’ (8:13), this angel brings good news. ἔχοντα εὐαγγέλιον αἰώνιον εὐαγγελίσαι ἐπὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, “having an eternal Good News to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth” — εὐαγγέλιον, gospel; αἰώνιος, from the time family: eternal, unchanging; γῆ, from the world family. Even now, the earth-dwellers are offered the gospel. καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔθνος καὶ φυλὴν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ λαόν, “and to every nation, tribe, language, and people.”

scripture.text: He said with a loud voice, “Fear the Lord, and give him glory; for the hour of his judgment has come. Worship him who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and the springs of waters!”
scripture.understanding: λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Φοβήθητε τὸν θεὸν καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν, “He said with a loud voice, ‘Fear the Lord, and give him glory’” — the call of 11:13 again: turn from the beast to the Creator. ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτοῦ, “for the hour of his judgment has come” — ὥρα, from the time family; κρίσις, from the judge family: judgement as an act, a trial in progress, as distinct from κρίμα, the verdict (17:1). καὶ προσκυνήσατε τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων, “Worship him who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and the springs of waters!” — γῆ, from the world family. The four realms struck by the first four trumpets: the Creator of all deserves the worship the beast demands.

scripture.text: Another, a second angel, followed, saying, “Babylon the great has fallen, which has made all the nations to drink of the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality.”
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος δεύτερος ἠκολούθησεν λέγων, “Another, a second angel, followed, saying” — ἄλλος, from the another family. Ἔπεσεν ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, “Babylon the great has fallen” — Isaiah's cry, ‘Fallen, fallen is Babylon’. Prophetic past tense: so certain it is as good as done. Babylon, the great city of chapters 17–18, is the world-system of power, wealth and pleasure opposed to God — Rome for John's readers. ἣ ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πεπότικεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, “which has made all the nations to drink of the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality” — θυμός, from the wrath family: here the passion of her immorality, which becomes the wine of God's wrath (v. 10).

scripture.text: Another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a great voice, “If anyone worships the beast and his image, and receives a mark on his forehead, or on his hand,
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος τρίτος ἠκολούθησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ, “Another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a great voice” — ἄλλος, from the another family. Εἴ τις προσκυνεῖ τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, “If anyone worships the beast and his image” — εἰκών, from the image family. καὶ λαμβάνει χάραγμα ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου αὐτοῦ ἢ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ, “and receives a mark on his forehead, or on his hand” — χάραγμα: the beast threatened death for refusing his mark (13:15); God warns of something worse for accepting it.

scripture.text: he also will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is prepared unmixed in the cup of his anger. He will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὐτὸς πίεται ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, “he also will drink of the wine of the wrath of God” — θυμός, from the wrath family: God's wrath poured out in its full intensity. Those who drank Babylon's wine (v. 8) must drink God's. τοῦ κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ, “which is prepared unmixed in the cup of his anger” — ὀργή, from the wrath family: settled, judicial anger. θυμός and ὀργή in one verse: passionate intensity and settled justice together. ἄκρατος, undiluted: ancient wine was mixed with water; this is not. καὶ βασανισθήσεται ἐν πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων ἁγίων καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου, “He will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb” — ἀρνίον, from the lamb family: the One they rejected is the witness of their judgement.

scripture.text: The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever. They have no rest day and night, those who worship the beast and his image, and whoever receives the mark of his name.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ καπνὸς τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώνων ἀναβαίνει, “The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever” — αἰών, from the time family and the world family: like the smoke of Sodom; the language of final, lasting judgement. Christians differ on whether it means unending conscious punishment or a final, irreversible destruction, but not on its seriousness. καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνάπαυσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, “They have no rest day and night” — ἀνάπαυσις, from the rest family; ἡμέρα, from the time family: the same words as the unceasing worship of the living creatures (4:8). οἱ προσκυνοῦντες τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, “those who worship the beast and his image” — εἰκών, from the image family.

scripture.text: Here is the perseverance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”
scripture.understanding: Ὧδε ἡ ὑπομονὴ τῶν ἁγίων ἐστίν, “Here is the perseverance of the saints” — ὑπομονή, from the endurance family, as in 13:10. The warnings of verses 9–11 are written to strengthen believers: it is better to suffer the beast's sword than God's wrath. οἱ τηροῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν πίστιν Ἰησοῦ, “those who keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus” — τηρέω, from the hold family: the marks of the woman's offspring (12:17). ‘The faith of Jesus’ is faith in Jesus, and faithfulness like His.

scripture.text: I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write, ‘Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.’” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them.”
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λεγούσης· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ νεκροὶ οἱ ἐν κυρίῳ ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἀπ᾽ ἄρτι, “Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on” — the second of the seven blessings. In a chapter about martyrdom, death in the Lord is called blessed. ναί, λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα, ἵνα ἀναπαήσονται ἐκ τῶν κόπων αὐτῶν, “that they may rest from their labors” — ἀναπαύω, from the rest family: the opposite of the beast-worshippers' ‘no rest’ (v. 11); κόπος, from the work family: wearying toil. τὰ γὰρ ἔργα αὐτῶν ἀκολουθεῖ μετ᾽ αὐτῶν, “for their works follow with them” — ἔργον, also from the work family: κόπος is the exhausting labour, ἔργον the deed that remains. Their toil ends; its fruit goes with them.

scripture.text: I looked, and behold, a white cloud; and on the cloud one sitting like a son of man, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ νεφέλη λευκή, “I looked, and behold, a white cloud” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην καθήμενον ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, “and on the cloud one sitting like a son of man” — Daniel's ‘one like a son of man’ coming with the clouds, as in 1:13: this is Christ. ἔχων ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ στέφανον χρυσοῦν, “having on his head a golden crown” — στέφανος, from the crown family: the victor's wreath. καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ δρέπανον ὀξύ, “and in his hand a sharp sickle” — δρέπανον, a harvesting hook: the Lord of the harvest.

scripture.text: Another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him who sat on the cloud, “Send your sickle, and reap; for the hour to reap has come; for the harvest of the earth is ripe!”
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ κράζων, “Another angel came out of the temple, crying” — ἄλλος, from the another family: the message comes from God's presence. Πέμψον τὸ δρέπανόν σου καὶ θέρισον, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα θερίσαι, “Send your sickle, and reap; for the hour to reap has come” — θερίζω, to reap grain; ὥρα, from the time family: the Father's appointed hour (Mark 13:32). ὅτι ἐξηράνθη ὁ θερισμὸς τῆς γῆς, “for the harvest of the earth is ripe!” — θερισμός; γῆ, from the world family. The grain harvest is most naturally the gathering of God's people, as Jesus described: ‘gather the wheat into my barn’.

scripture.text: He who sat on the cloud thrust his sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῆς νεφέλης τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, “He who sat on the cloud thrust his sickle on the earth” — the Son of Man reaps in person; γῆ, from the world family. καὶ ἐθερίσθη ἡ γῆ, “and the earth was reaped” — one swift stroke: the gathering is complete. No judgement is described here; the second harvest is different.

scripture.text: Another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven. He also had a sharp sickle.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “Another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven” — ἄλλος, from the another family. ἔχων καὶ αὐτὸς δρέπανον ὀξύ, “He also had a sharp sickle” — a second harvest, carried out by an angel, as Jesus said: ‘the reapers are angels’ (Matthew 13:39).

scripture.text: Another angel came out from the altar, he who has power over fire, and he called with a great voice to him who had the sharp sickle, saying, “Send your sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, for the earth’s grapes are fully ripe!”
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐκ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ὁ ἔχων ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρός, “Another angel came out from the altar, he who has power over fire” — ἄλλος, from the another family; ἐξουσία, from the power family; θυσιαστήριον: the altar of the martyrs' cry (6:9) and the saints' prayers (8:3–5). This harvest answers their prayers. Πέμψον σου τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ καὶ τρύγησον τοὺς βότρυας τῆς ἀμπέλου τῆς γῆς, “Send your sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth” — τρυγάω, to gather grapes; γῆ, from the world family. Not the true Vine (John 15) but the vine of the earth. ὅτι ἤκμασαν αἱ σταφυλαὶ αὐτῆς, “for the earth’s grapes are fully ripe!” — evil has come to full ripeness.

scripture.text: The angel thrust his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vintage of the earth, and threw it into the great wine press of the wrath of God.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν, “The angel thrust his sickle into the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. καὶ ἐτρύγησεν τὴν ἄμπελον τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν ληνὸν τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν μέγαν, “and gathered the vintage of the earth, and threw it into the great wine press of the wrath of God” — ληνός, a winepress; θυμός, from the wrath family. Isaiah saw God treading the winepress of judgement alone; Joel called the nations to the valley of decision, ‘for the winepress is full’.

scripture.text: The wine press was trodden outside of the city, and blood came out of the wine press, even to the bridles of the horses, as far as one thousand six hundred stadia.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐπατήθη ἡ ληνὸς ἔξωθεν τῆς πόλεως, “The wine press was trodden outside of the city” — outside the city, where Jesus suffered (Hebrews 13:12): those who refuse His suffering for them face their own. καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αἷμα ἐκ τῆς ληνοῦ ἄχρι τῶν χαλινῶν τῶν ἵππων, “and blood came out of the wine press, even to the bridles of the horses” — a deliberately horrifying picture. ἀπὸ σταδίων χιλίων ἑξακοσίων, “as far as one thousand six hundred stadia” — about 300 kilometres, roughly the length of Palestine; 1,600 is 4 × 4 × 100: the four corners of the earth. Universal, total judgement.

visualMeditations.title: The Lamb on Mount Zion
visualMeditations.image: Picture, after the beasts rising from sea and land, a different scene: a Lamb standing on a mountain, and with Him a vast, ordered company, the names of the Lamb and His Father written on every forehead. From heaven comes a sound like a waterfall, like thunder, like a great choir of harps, singing a song only they can learn.
visualMeditations.meaning: “I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him a number, one hundred forty-four thousand, having his name, and the name of his Father, written on their foreheads” (v. 1). “These are those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes” (v. 4). The beast's followers bear his mark; the Lamb's followers bear His name.

visualMeditations.title: The Eternal Gospel in Mid-Heaven
visualMeditations.image: Picture an angel flying high across the sky, visible to every nation, carrying a message for every tribe and language: ‘Fear God! Give Him glory! Worship the Creator!’
visualMeditations.meaning: “I saw an angel flying in mid heaven, having an eternal Good News to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth, and to every nation, tribe, language, and people” (v. 6). Even on the edge of judgement, God's last word to the world is good news.

visualMeditations.title: Rest and No Rest
visualMeditations.image: Picture two scenes side by side. In one, smoke rises day and night from those who chose the beast; they have no rest. In the other, believers who died for Jesus lie down at last, their tired faces at peace, while all their works walk behind them like a faithful company.
visualMeditations.meaning: “They have no rest day and night, those who worship the beast and his image” (v. 11). “Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them” (v. 13).

visualMeditations.title: Two Harvests
visualMeditations.image: Picture a golden wheat field and the Son of Man on a white cloud, sweeping His sickle once across it, gathering the grain home. Then picture a vineyard, its grapes heavy and dark, cut by an angel and thrown into a vast winepress outside the city — and red streaming out for miles.
visualMeditations.meaning: “He who sat on the cloud thrust his sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped” (v. 16). “The angel... gathered the vintage of the earth, and threw it into the great wine press of the wrath of God” (v. 19). Every life will be harvested. The question is whether you are wheat gathered home, or grapes thrown into the winepress.

structure.label: The Lamb and the 144,000 (v. 1-5)
structure.body: John sees the Lamb on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who bear His and His Father's names; a heavenly sound like waters, thunder and harps sings a new song that only the redeemed can learn; they are spiritually pure, follow the Lamb wherever He goes, are firstfruits to God, and no lie is in their mouths.

structure.label: Three Angels (v. 6-13)
structure.body: One angel proclaims an eternal gospel to every nation: fear God, give Him glory, worship the Creator, for the hour of judgement has come; a second announces the fall of Babylon the great; a third warns that whoever worships the beast and receives its mark will drink the wine of God's wrath and have no rest; here is the endurance of the saints; a voice from heaven blesses those who die in the Lord, who rest from their labours.

structure.label: Two Harvests (v. 14-20)
structure.body: One like a son of man on a white cloud with a golden crown and a sharp sickle reaps the ripe harvest of the earth; another angel gathers the ripe grapes of the earth's vine and throws them into the great winepress of God's wrath, which is trodden outside the city, and blood flows for 1,600 stadia.

sections.heading: The Lamb and His Army
paragraphs: After the terrifying beasts of chapter 13, John sees the answer: “I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him a number, one hundred forty-four thousand, having his name, and the name of his Father, written on their foreheads” (v. 1). The dragon stood on the shifting sand of the sea (13:1); the Lamb stands on the mountain of God. The beast's followers bear his mark (13:16); the Lamb's people bear His name. Hebrews says believers have already “come to Mount Zion, and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem” (Hebrews 12:22).

They sing a new song that only they can learn, because only the redeemed know what redemption is (v. 3). They are described in four ways. They “were not defiled with women, for they are virgins” (v. 4): in the language of the prophets and Revelation, idolatry is sexual unfaithfulness, and Babylon is a prostitute (ch. 17). They have kept themselves pure for Christ, as Paul says, “I married you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ” (2 Corinthians 11:2). They “follow the Lamb wherever he goes” — including the way of the cross. They are “the first fruits to God and to the Lamb” (v. 4), offered to God as the pledge of the full harvest. And “In their mouth was found no lie” (v. 5): they refused the beast's great lie.

sections.heading: The Gospel, the Fall and the Warning
paragraphs: Three angels fly through heaven with three messages. The first carries “an eternal Good News to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth, and to every nation, tribe, language, and people” (v. 6): “Fear the Lord, and give him glory; for the hour of his judgment has come. Worship him who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and the springs of waters!” (v. 7). Even at this late hour, God offers the gospel to the whole world. Jesus said, “This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come” (Matthew 24:14).

The second angel announces, “Babylon the great has fallen” (v. 8). This is the first mention of Babylon, the great city of chapters 17–18 — the world-system of power, wealth and seduction, embodied in John's day by Rome. Her fall is announced before it is described: God's verdict is certain.

The third angel gives the most solemn warning in the Bible: whoever worships the beast “also will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is prepared unmixed in the cup of his anger” (v. 10). Both words for wrath appear: θυμός, the full intensity of God's anger, and ὀργή, His settled judicial wrath. The cup is ‘unmixed’ — not diluted with mercy. “The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever” (v. 11). Faithful Christians have read this in different ways — as unending conscious punishment, or as total and final destruction — but none can read it lightly. Jesus said, “One who believes in the Son has eternal life, but one who disobeys the Son won’t see life, but the wrath of God remains on him” (John 3:36).

sections.heading: Blessed Are the Dead
paragraphs: Why such a terrible warning? It is for the church: “Here is the perseverance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus” (v. 12). Believers under pressure to worship the beast must weigh the cost: the beast can take their lives, but God holds their eternity. It is better to face the beast's sword than God's wrath.

Then comes one of the most comforting verses in Scripture: “Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them” (v. 13). Those who worship the beast have no rest; those who die in the Lord rest. Their κόπος, their weary toil, is over; their ἔργα, their works of faith and love, go with them. Paul says, “your labor is not in vain in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 15:58).

This blessing is especially for martyrs, but it belongs to all who die ‘in the Lord’ — united to Christ by faith. Death for a believer is not defeat but rest. “There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God” (Hebrews 4:9).

sections.heading: The Grain Harvest and the Grape Harvest
paragraphs: The chapter ends with two harvests. First, “one sitting like a son of man” on a white cloud, wearing a golden crown, reaps the earth with a sharp sickle (vv. 14–16). This is Christ Himself. The grain harvest is most naturally the gathering of His people at the end of the age: Jesus told of the harvest in which the master says, “gather the wheat into my barn” (Matthew 13:30). Some see both harvests as judgement, but the difference between them is striking: the first is reaped by Christ, and nothing is said of wrath.

The second harvest is a vintage: an angel from the altar of the martyrs' prayers gathers “the clusters of the vine of the earth” (v. 18) and throws them “into the great wine press of the wrath of God” (v. 19). Isaiah saw God treading the winepress of judgement; Joel called the nations to the valley of decision, where the winepress is full. The ‘vine of the earth’ is the opposite of Christ, the true Vine.

“The wine press was trodden outside of the city, and blood came out of the wine press, even to the bridles of the horses, as far as one thousand six hundred stadia” (v. 20). The picture is meant to horrify. Outside the city is where Jesus suffered God's judgement for sinners (Hebrews 13:12). Those who will not take shelter in His death outside the city will face judgement there themselves. Every life will be harvested; the gospel of verse 6 is still the way to be gathered as wheat.

ntConnection.heading: The Harvest at the End of the Age
paragraphs: Jesus explained His parable of the wheat and the weeds: “The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels” (Matthew 13:39). He also said, “Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes, and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already” (John 4:35) — the harvest begins now, through the gospel.
James calls believers firstfruits: “Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures” (James 1:18) — like the 144,000 of verse 4.
And the rest of verse 13 echoes Hebrews: “For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his” (Hebrews 4:10).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “a maiden; by implication, an unmarried daughter.” παρθένος usually means an unmarried young woman; here it is applied to the whole company of the redeemed. Throughout the Bible, idolatry is spiritual adultery, and God's people are His bride. To be ‘virgins’ is to have kept oneself for Christ alone — not seduced by Babylon the prostitute or the beast. Paul's hope was ‘to present you as a pure virgin to Christ’ (2 Corinthians 11:2).

Strong's: “a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. the (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively).” ἀπαρχή was the first portion of the harvest, offered to God as a thanksgiving and a pledge that the rest would follow. Christ is ‘the first fruits of those who are asleep’ (1 Corinthians 15:20), and believers are ‘a kind of first fruits of his creatures’ (James 1:18). The 144,000 are firstfruits ‘to God and to the Lamb’: the beginning and guarantee of a far greater harvest.

Strong's: “perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well).” αἰώνιος, from the time family, comes from αἰών, an age: belonging to the age to come, without end. It describes eternal life, eternal judgement, the eternal Spirit — and here the ‘eternal Good News’, the only place the gospel is called eternal. Empires rise and fall; the beast has forty-two months; but the gospel does not change.

Strong's: “a gathering hook (especially for harvesting).” δρέπανον, a curved blade for cutting grain or grapes, appears seven times in verses 14–19 and nowhere else in the New Testament except Mark 4:29, where Jesus says that when the grain is ripe, the farmer ‘puts forth the sickle, because the harvest has come’. In Revelation the Son of Man holds the sickle: the harvest of history is in His hands.

Strong's: “a trough, i.e. wine-vat.” ληνός was a stone trough where grapes were trodden underfoot and the juice ran out through a channel. Isaiah 63 pictures God coming from Edom with garments stained red, having trodden the winepress of His wrath alone. Revelation 19:15 says Christ ‘treads the wine press of the fierceness of the wrath of God’. The judgement that Christ bore for His people on the cross, He will execute on those who reject Him.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit sets two destinies before you — and urges you to choose life.

items.title: Follow the Lamb Wherever He Goes
items.body: The redeemed “follow the Lamb wherever he goes” (v. 4). The Spirit asks you to follow Jesus not only where it is easy, but where it is costly — into humility, sacrifice and even suffering. He leads to Mount Zion.

items.title: Rest Is Coming
items.body: “Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord... that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them” (v. 13). If you are weary from serving God, the Spirit speaks this ‘yes’ over you. Your labour is not wasted. Rest is coming, and your faithful works will go with you.

items.title: Proclaim the Eternal Gospel
items.body: God's last call to the world is good news: ‘Fear God, give Him glory, worship the Creator’ (vv. 6–7). The Spirit wants you to carry that message urgently and lovingly to every nation, tribe, language and people — and to your neighbour.

audit.title: The Purity Check
audit.body: Have you kept yourself spiritually faithful to Christ, or have you been seduced by the world's idols of money, sex and power (v. 4)?

audit.title: The Truth Check
audit.body: Is there any lie in your mouth — in what you say about yourself, others or God (v. 5)?

audit.title: The Harvest Check
audit.body: If the harvest came today, would you be gathered as wheat into the Lord's barn (vv. 15–16)?

practices.title: Share the Eternal Gospel
practices.body: Write a short, clear summary of the gospel in your own words, based on verses 6–7 and John 3:16. This week, share it with one person who does not know Jesus.

practices.title: Prepare to Rest
practices.body: Write down the ‘works’ you hope will follow you (v. 13) — people you have served, faith you have shared, love you have shown. Then choose one work of love to do this week that will last into eternity.

prayerReflection: “Lamb of God, standing on Mount Zion, thank You that You have redeemed me and written Your name and Your Father's name on me. Teach me the new song of the redeemed. Keep me pure for You, free from every idol, and let no lie be found in my mouth. Help me follow You wherever You go. Thank You for the eternal gospel. Make me a messenger of it to every nation, tribe, language and people, calling them to fear God, give Him glory and worship the Creator. Lord, I tremble at the cup of Your wrath, and I thank You that You drank it for me. Give me the endurance of the saints, to keep God's commandments and the faith of Jesus. Thank You that those who die in You are blessed, and that they rest from their labours, and their works follow them. Son of Man on the white cloud, when You reap the earth, gather me with Your wheat into Your barn. Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Ruth Gleaning at the Harvest
storyConnections.summary: Ruth, a Moabite widow who had chosen Israel's God, went to glean in the barley fields of Bethlehem and happened on the field of Boaz. Boaz, her kinsman-redeemer, treated her kindly, told his reapers to leave extra grain for her, and later redeemed her and married her. From their line came David — and Jesus. The harvest in the Bible is a time of gathering and redemption: the Lord of the harvest gathers the outsider into His family.

storyConnections.title: Fallen Is Babylon
storyConnections.summary: Isaiah saw a terrible vision of invaders coming against Babylon. A watchman on the tower kept looking, day and night, until he saw a chariot of horsemen and cried out, ‘Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.’ Babylon, the proud empire that had crushed Jerusalem and exiled God's people, would itself fall. Revelation takes up the same cry for the Babylon of its day — and of every day.

storyConnections.title: The One Who Treads the Winepress Alone
storyConnections.summary: Isaiah saw a warrior coming from Edom, His garments stained crimson. Asked why His clothes were red like one who treads the winepress, He answered, ‘I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the peoples no one was with me... their lifeblood is sprinkled on my garments.’ He had come to bring judgement on His enemies and redemption for His people. Revelation applies this picture to the final judgement — and in 19:13 the Rider is clothed in a robe dipped in blood.
